_schema: Filled in by an agent from the yurigana repo's eval runs; sites/yurigana.html renders all of it.
updated: date measured (YYYY-MM-DD). commit: yurigana commit the numbers are from.
columns: one per test set. id is the key into each row's scores; lower: true when smaller is better; fmt 'about' prints 'about N'; words: how many words the set scores; note: one plain sentence.
rows: kind is 'ours' (yurigana), 'other' (a tool it's compared with) or 'ceiling' (not a rival, e.g. an LLM; never marked best). A missing score is null.

examples: real sentences from the sets where yurigana is right and others are wrong. text is the plain sentence; word is the kanji word as it appears in text (first occurrence is the one scored); gold is the right reading; readings maps a row name to what that system read (omit a system that wasn't run). why: one short sentence on what decides the reading. Set placeholder: true on made-up entries; the page marks them and the agent deletes them.

columns.name: Modern books
columns.note: The books' own furigana over post-war novels and light novels by authors yurigana never trained on. A private library, so the set isn't published.

columns.name: Modern, hard words
columns.note: The same books, only words that can be read two or more ways.

columns.name: Older books
columns.note: 300 sentences of NDL's huriganacorpus-aozora: human furigana, mostly pre-war Aozora Bunko texts.

columns.name: Older, hard words
columns.note: The same sentences, only words that can be read two or more ways.

columns.name: Tatoeba B2
columns.note: 27,000 sentences whose answers are MeCab + IPAdic's own furigana, so MeCab + IPAdic scores high here.

columns.name: Joyo-Kanji-Yomi
columns.note: Three checked sentences for every reading of every Jōyō kanji, rare ones included.

columns.name: Wrong words per book
columns.note: Kanji words read wrong in a typical 19,000-word book, before its own furigana fixes any.

rows.name: Claude Opus
rows.note: Annotating the same sentences blind, as a ceiling.

examples.text: 人気のない道を一人で歩いた。
examples.why: Followed by のない, 人気 means people around, not popularity.

examples.text: 机の上に三本の鉛筆があった。
examples.why: 本 after 三 voices to ぼん, a counter rule.
